name: Ghost-Cart
tagline: **Location-aware AI shopping assistant** — Claude autonomously decides what to restock, when to nudge you to go shopping, and what to say. Built on a Node.js gateway + Python FastAPI brain + React Native app.

techStack.technology: React Native, Expo SDK 54, Expo Router, Zustand, AsyncStorage
Node.js 20+, Express 4, Zod, node-cache, Helmet, Axios
Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, cachetools, Anthropic SDK
Expo Location, Google Places Nearby Search API

architecture.overview:
Ghost-Cart is a grocery assistant that goes beyond a simple list app — it actively reasons about your shopping needs using Claude AI.

| Capability | How it works |
|---|---|
| **Chat to build your list** | Type naturally ("high-protein breakfast") — Claude suggests items and adds them |
| **Smart store filtering** | Walk into a store and the list automatically hides items that store doesn't carry |
| **Restock Agent** | Claude scans your purchase history and autonomously decides what to add back |
| **Nudge Agent** | After 12h in the background, Claude decides whether to send a push notification and writes the copy itself |
| **GPS store detection** | Polls every 30s; detects when you enter a known store and triggers agents automatically |

The two **agentic** features (Restock + Nudge) use `tool_choice="auto"` with a while-loop — Claude runs freely until it decides it's done, with no hard-coded rules or thresholds.

keyDecisions.what: Three separate services: Node.js gateway, Python brain, React Native mobile — not a monolith
keyDecisions.why: Isolates concerns; each service has a single job. Gateway handles I/O and validation, brain handles AI, mobile handles UX. Independent deployable units.

keyDecisions.what: Brain accepts requests only from the gateway via an internal network; it has no public URL that works without the secret header
keyDecisions.why: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` never leaves the brain process. Even if the gateway is fully compromised, the AI key cannot be extracted.

keyDecisions.what: `X-Internal-Secret` shared header, not JWT or OAuth
keyDecisions.why: Simple, stateless, no token expiry to manage. The only consumer of the brain is the gateway — a lightweight secret is the right tool for a trusted internal channel.

keyDecisions.what: Node.js for gateway, Python for brain
keyDecisions.why: Node.js handles high-throughput async I/O well; Python has the best AI/ML ecosystem. Using the right language per job outweighs the overhead of a polyglot stack.

keyDecisions.what: Direct Anthropic Python SDK (`anthropic.AsyncAnthropic`) — no LangChain or wrapper
keyDecisions.why: LangChain adds ~150 MB of abstraction designed for multi-model chains and RAG pipelines. Ghost-Cart calls a single Claude endpoint; the direct SDK is leaner, typed, and easier to debug.

keyDecisions.what: `tool_choice="auto"` with a `while` loop for Restock and Nudge agents
keyDecisions.why: Gives Claude genuine autonomy — it decides what to call and when to stop. Code provides tools and context; Claude provides judgment. This is the line between "AI as function call" and "AI as agent."

keyDecisions.what: `tool_choice="tool"` (forced) for the Intent Filter
keyDecisions.why: The Intent Filter output must be deterministic and code-controlled. Forcing the tool call guarantees the response shape; Claude doesn't need to decide whether to call it.

keyDecisions.what: `send_nudge` and `skip_nudge` as deliberate opposites; both require a reason
keyDecisions.why: No silent no-op path. Claude must make an explicit binary decision and provide reasoning — this produces a clean audit trail in logs and forces deliberate behaviour rather than drift.

keyDecisions.what: Urgency thresholds (low 5–9d / medium 10–13d / high 14+d) live in `input_schema` description fields
keyDecisions.why: Business logic belongs where Claude reads it. Changing a threshold means editing the schema, not the application code — no redeployment of conditional logic required.

keyDecisions.what: Full context (purchase history, days elapsed, current list) sent on every agent request — no server-side session state
keyDecisions.why: Simpler, cheaper, more reliable. Each request is self-contained; no state drift between calls, no session storage to maintain. Horizontal scaling is trivial.

keyDecisions.what: `MAX_ITERATIONS = 10` hard cap + hardcoded fallback result if Claude never calls a tool
keyDecisions.why: Prevents infinite loops and runaway API spend. If Claude produces no tool call after the cap, the caller still gets a valid deterministic response — the system never hangs.

keyDecisions.what: `node-cache` in gateway (10 min TTL) + `TTLCache` in brain
keyDecisions.why: Cache hits at the gateway never reach the brain or Claude API — that's the primary cost lever. The brain cache provides a second line for any requests that bypass the gateway. Projected ~60% fewer API calls at 60% hit rate.

keyDecisions.what: Structured JSON to stdout — no logging database
keyDecisions.why: Logs are a stream, not a table. Railway captures stdout automatically; a Logtail HTTP drain makes all JSON fields (`input_tokens`, `latency_ms`, `request_id`) instantly searchable. Writing logs to Postgres would be slow, expensive, and the wrong query pattern.

keyDecisions.what: `X-Request-ID` generated at gateway, forwarded to brain, stored in `ContextVar`, logged on every event
keyDecisions.why: A single `grep` across both services reconstructs a complete user action — from the gateway request through all Claude iterations — without cross-referencing timestamps or guessing.

keyDecisions.what: `re.sub` strips `` ```json``` `` fences before every `json.loads()` call
keyDecisions.why: Claude reliably wraps JSON in markdown code blocks even when prompted not to. `json.loads()` fails on the backtick with a cryptic error. Stripping first is a defensive pattern that belongs in every service that parses Claude's output.

keyDecisions.what: React Native + Expo SDK 54 with Expo Router
keyDecisions.why: Single codebase for iOS and Android; Expo handles native modules, build tooling, and OTA updates. Expo Router gives file-based navigation consistent with modern web conventions.

keyDecisions.what: Zustand + AsyncStorage
keyDecisions.why: Zustand is lighter than Redux with no boilerplate. AsyncStorage gives offline-first persistence — shopping list and history survive app restarts with no backend dependency in the MVP.

keyDecisions.what: Haversine distance formula, polled every 30 seconds
keyDecisions.why: Cross-platform and permission-light compared to OS geofencing APIs. 30s polling is fine-grained enough for store entry detection without draining battery. Deterministic and easy to test.

keyDecisions.what: EAS (Expo Application Services) for builds; APK for Android testers, Expo Go for iOS until Apple Developer enrollment
keyDecisions.why: EAS manages Android/iOS build toolchains without local Xcode or Android Studio setup. APK distribution is immediate for Android; Expo Go covers iOS without the $99/yr enrollment cost for early-stage testing.

keyDecisions.what: `test_cases.json` with 12 input/expected-decision pairs (TC-01→TC-12)
keyDecisions.why: AI agents need behavior specs, not just unit tests. Each case defines what Claude *should decide* given a specific context — a PM-level contract that doubles as a regression suite.

reflections.call: Use LangChain to talk to Claude
reflections.whyWrong: LangChain is built for chaining multiple models and RAG pipelines — ~150 MB of abstraction for a single Claude endpoint. Its own abstraction layer adds a failure surface and makes the integration harder to debug.
reflections.correction: Used the Anthropic Python SDK directly (`anthropic.AsyncAnthropic`). One dependency, fully typed, no layer between the code and Claude's API behaviour.

reflections.call: "The app has nothing agentic — I've failed as an AI PM"
reflections.whyWrong: The framing was wrong, not the facts. The GPS→store detection→intent filter chain was a perception-decision-action loop — just shallow, because *code* was making all decisions for Claude. Real diagnosis: "Claude is a function call, not an agent."
reflections.correction: Built the Restock Agent with `tool_choice="auto"` and a while-loop. Then the Nudge Agent. Two genuinely agentic features, designed from first principles.

reflections.call: "I've already integrated GitHub — Claude can push directly"
reflections.whyWrong: Claude Code can't authenticate to GitHub on your behalf. OAuth requires the user to run the flow in their own terminal — Claude only picks up credentials already stored.
reflections.correction: Ran `gh auth login` and `railway login` manually. Claude then used the stored tokens for all subsequent git and Railway operations.

reflections.call: Build an MCP to query Walmart's real inventory database
reflections.whyWrong: Walmart has no public API for real-time inventory. Designing a feature spec around a data source that doesn't exist is a PM mistake — validate supply before building the feature.
reflections.correction: Moved to roadmap with a note that a mock/simulated inventory endpoint covers the demo and the technical pattern.

reflections.call: "Do we need a database to store logs?"
reflections.whyWrong: Logs are an append-only stream, not relational data. Writing token counts and latency to Postgres would be slow, expensive at scale, and the wrong query pattern — logs need full-text search, not SQL joins.
reflections.correction: stdout → Railway captures it → Logtail HTTP log drain. No extra DB, no schema. All structured fields (`input_tokens`, `latency_ms`, `request_id`) immediately searchable.

reflections.call: Plan on TestFlight for 2 iOS testers right away
reflections.whyWrong: TestFlight requires the Apple Developer Program ($99/yr). Without enrollment you can't upload builds, create TestFlight groups, or distribute to real devices outside Expo Go.
reflections.correction: iOS testers use Expo Go (scan QR, free, immediate). Android testers get an EAS APK link. TestFlight is an explicit roadmap item with its prerequisite stated.

reflections.whyWrong: EAS's `--id` flag expects a UUID, not a slug. The command silently wrote `"projectId": "ghost-cart"` into `app.json`, causing GraphQL errors on every EAS build with no helpful error message.
reflections.correction: Removed the bad block and ran `eas init --non-interactive --force`, which generated the proper UUID (`0bfcd389-eca1-4cd6-a3eb-dd99f7d2ee08`).

reflections.call: `cd brain && railway up` to deploy just the brain
reflections.whyWrong: Railway always uploads from the git root regardless of shell directory. Running from `brain/` still sent the entire monorepo; Railway couldn't detect the language without a root directory configured.
reflections.correction: Set `rootDirectory: "brain"` and `rootDirectory: "gateway"` per service via the Railway GraphQL API; deployed from repo root with `railway up --service <ID>`.

reflections.call: Assumed `railway service create` was a valid CLI command
reflections.whyWrong: Railway CLI v4 has no `service create` subcommand. Service management beyond basic deploys requires the dashboard or GraphQL API — a gap that only surfaces when you try it.
reflections.correction: Created the gateway service via the Railway GraphQL `serviceCreate` mutation, then used the returned ID for all subsequent deploys.

reflections.call: Started the EAS Android build without a `.npmrc`
reflections.whyWrong: Expo SDK 54 pins `react@19.1.0` but an indirect dep (`react-dom@19.2.4`) requires `react@^19.2.4`. The EAS build server fails with a peer conflict that doesn't appear in local dev.
reflections.correction: Added `mobile/.npmrc` with `legacy-peer-deps=true`. EAS Build picks it up automatically — no config workarounds needed.

reflections.call: Assumed Claude would return raw JSON with no special handling
reflections.whyWrong: Claude often wraps JSON in ` ```json ``` ` markdown blocks even when the prompt asks for JSON. `json.loads()` fails on the backtick — a silent 502 in production that's hard to trace.
reflections.correction: Added `re.sub` stripping before every `json.loads()` call in `ai.py`. Pattern documented in CLAUDE.md for all future services.

reflections.call: Asked about "skills.md" as a standard Claude Code filename
reflections.whyWrong: There is no file called `skills.md`. Treating an assumed filename as a known spec without verifying first is a gap between confidence and knowledge.
reflections.correction: Looked up the real format from existing plugin files: it's `SKILL.md` (uppercase) inside `.claude/skills/<name>/`, with YAML frontmatter controlling invocation mode and tool access.

reflections.call: Create a PR containing the HTML artifact file
reflections.whyWrong: An HTML file renders as raw markup in GitHub's file viewer and doesn't integrate with the docs people actually read. A browser deliverable isn't useful as a repo source file.
reflections.correction: Updated `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the project plan with markdown tables instead — embedded in the docs that already exist, no orphan file.
